---

## Sources on Cornelius Driscoll — 7 attached, 3 findings

**Profile facts:** Birth 1814, Ireland; Marriage 9 June 1849, Sherbrooke, Canada East; Residence 1851 & 1861 Sherbrooke, Canada East; Burial, St. Patrick's Cemetery, Sherbrooke (no death date recorded).

---

### Finding 1 — Indexing Error: Marriage date

**Source:** "Quebec, Vital and Church Records (Drouin Collection), 1621–1968"

The index records the marriage year as **1845**; the profile records **1849**. The day (9 June), the bride (Margaret Hayes), and the parish (St. Patrick's, Sherbrooke) all match — only the year differs. A single-digit misread in a handwritten register is the likely cause.

**Action:** Open the original register page on FamilySearch (the collection has images) and confirm which year appears. If it reads 1849, submit an index correction. Keep the source attached regardless.

---

### Finding 2 — Ambiguous: Possible misattribution or indexing error on 1851 Census residence

**Source:** "Census of Canada East, 1851"

The index gives the residence as **Melbourne**, Canada East; the profile records **Sherbrooke**. These are two separate municipalities in the Eastern Townships — not minor drift. The name and birthplace (Ireland) match, but the place is a substantive disagreement.

**Action:** Examine the original 1851 returns for both Melbourne and Sherbrooke before deciding. Do not detach until the original confirms whether this is a different Cornelius Driscoll.

---

### Finding 3 — Source Conflict: Death date (needs conflict-resolution)

Two sources directly contradict each other on the death date:

- **"Quebec, Catholic Parish Registers, 1621–1979"** (burial record, images available): Death **April 1878**, burial **14 April 1878**, St. Patrick's Cemetery, Sherbrooke.
- **"Quebec, Civil Registration Deaths, 1867–1900"** (index only, no images): Death **2 February 1885** — nearly seven years later.

Both fit the person in name, place, and birth year (1814). The profile records no death date, so neither conflicts with the profile directly, but the two sources conflict with each other. **Take this to the conflict-resolution workflow.** Neither source should be detached on current evidence.

---

### Unchecked Source

One contributor-uploaded headstone photograph (St. Patrick's Cemetery) has no indexed record behind it and cannot be verified through FamilySearch's record system. If the death date conflict is being worked, the photograph is worth examining — but its label likely echoes the tree rather than independently corroborating either date.

---

**No impossible-date warnings** on the project tree. FamilySearch's profile quality score is **0.94 (Green)**. The two-year birth year gap between sources (1814 vs. 1816) is ordinary census variance and was excluded from findings.

---

### Finding 1 — Misattributed source (most serious)
**"Minnesota State Census, 1885"** — [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:HOLE-003](https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:HOLE-003)

This source does **not** belong on this profile. The indexed record names a Christian Hole born **1852** in Norway, living in **Aurdal, Otter Tail County**, with a wife named Bergit and a child Nils. Christian P. Hole was born **1875** — he would have been ten years old in 1885 and could not be the head of household described. The birth year is off by 23 years, the county is wrong (Otter Tail vs. Polk), and the household is an entirely different family.

This same record is already correctly attached to **KD96-WX7** (Christian Hole, born 1852, Aurdal, Otter Tail County), where it fits perfectly.

**Action:** Detach this source from Christian P. Hole's profile. It belongs exclusively to KD96-WX7.

### Finding 2 — Indexing error
**"Minnesota Death Index, 1908–2002"** — [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:HOLE-002](https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:HOLE-002)

The indexed death year is **1954**; the profile records **1945**. All other fields agree (name, birth year 1875, death date 10 June, death place Erskine, Polk County). Because this is an index-only entry, the discrepancy must be resolved against the original death certificate.

**Action:** Locate the Minnesota death certificate. If it confirms 1945, submit a correction to the FamilySearch index entry. Keep the source attached otherwise.

---

- **Uploaded memory (funeral card):** No ARK, so no independent verification possible. It cannot corroborate the death year on its own.

subagents.description: Source evaluation for conflicting census birth years

output.text_response:
This question — two sources disagreeing about Christian's birth year (1900 census: 1875 vs. 1885 state census: 1852) — falls outside source-evaluation's scope. Source evaluation audits whether sources are correctly attached to a profile and flags indexing or transcription errors in individual records. It does not adjudicate between two sources that both appear genuine but give conflicting information.

**What you need is conflict-resolution.** That agent is designed exactly for this: it weighs competing sources against each other, applies the GPS preponderance hierarchy, and writes a rationale for which evidence is more reliable. It will consider factors like:

- Who provided the birth year in each record (self-report vs. someone else reporting)?
- How close in time was each record to the birth event?
- What are the informant's likely knowledge and motivation?
- Are there corroborating sources that support one figure over the other?

If you'd like, say **"resolve this conflict"** and I'll route you to the conflict-resolution agent to work through the 1875 vs. 1852 birth year discrepancy for Christian.

## Sources on Cornelius Driscoll (GJ72-9WD) — 7 Attached, 3 Findings

---

### 1. ⚠️ Worst — Death Year Conflict Between Two Records

**Quebec, Catholic Parish Registers (burial, DRIS-003) vs. Quebec, Civil Registration Deaths (DRIS-004)**

The burial register records burial on **14 April 1878** and death in April 1878. The civil death registration records death on **2 February 1885** — seven years later. Both share the same name (Cornelius Driscoll), birth year (1814), birthplace (Ireland), and district (Sherbrooke). The profile currently carries no death date, so there is no third anchor to resolve this.

**Action:** Take both records to the **conflict-resolution** workflow. Do not detach either record until that review determines whether one belongs to a different Cornelius Driscoll in the same parish.

---

### 2. Indexing/Transcription Error — Marriage Year Off by One Digit

**Quebec, Vital and Church Records (Drouin Collection), 1621–1968 (DRIS-002)**

Indexed marriage date: **9 June 1845**. Profile records: **9 June 1849**. Day and month are identical; only the final year-digit differs. Name, spouse (Margaret Hayes), and church (St. Patrick's, Sherbrooke) all match the profile exactly.

**Action:** Re-read the original page (collection has images). If the register reads 1849, use FamilySearch's index-correction path. Keep the source attached — it is good evidence with one potentially bad field.

---

### 3. Indexed Residence Disagrees with the Profile

**Census of Canada East, 1851 (DRIS-005)**

Indexed residence: **Melbourne, Canada East**. Profile records: **Sherbrooke, Canada East**. These are distinct townships — not merely a difference in precision. No household detail (spouse, age) is available to confirm or rule out the identification. The collection is database-only; no images are accessible through FamilySearch.

**Action:** Re-read the underlying census schedule through Library and Archives Canada. If the schedule reads Melbourne, update the profile's 1851 residence fact; if it reads Sherbrooke, submit an index correction. Do not detach before consulting the original.

---

### Not a Finding, But Worth Noting

The baptism record ("Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915") gives **12 March 1814, Skibbereen, Cork, Ireland** — more precise than the profile's vague "1814, Ireland." No conflict, but the profile's birth conclusion could be improved by adopting the specific date and place from that register.

Here is what the source-evaluation agent found on **Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2)**:

---

## Source Audit — 4 sources checked, 2 findings

### Finding 1 — Indexing Error (keep the source, fix the index)
**"Minnesota Death Index, 1908-2002"**

The indexed death year is **1954**, but the profile records **1945**. Everything else — birth year 1875, birthplace Norway, death place Erskine, Polk County, Minnesota, and the month/day (10 June) — matches perfectly. This is a single-field transcription error, almost certainly in the index itself.

**Action:** Locate the original death certificate and submit a correction through FamilySearch's index-correction path. Keep the source attached.

---

### Finding 2 — Misattributed Source (detach it)
**"Minnesota State Census, 1885"**

The census record names a Christian Hole born **1852** in Norway, living in **Otter Tail County** with wife Bergit and child Nils. Christian P. Hole was born in **1875**, meaning he would have been only ~10 years old in 1885 — not a household head with a wife and child. The birth year differs by 23 years, the county differs, and neither the spouse nor child names match anything on the profile.

This record is a strong match for **Christian Hole (KD96-WX7)** — another man in the tree, born 1852 in Norway, who died 1919 in Otter Tail County, and whose profile already holds the correct connection.

**Action:** Detach the 1885 Minnesota census source from Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2). It belongs to Christian Hole (KD96-WX7).

---

### Also Noted (not errors, but worth knowing)
- One contributor-uploaded item ("Hole family photograph and funeral card") has no readable record ID and could not be verified through indexed records.
- FamilySearch's own checklist flags: **marriage has no tagged sources**, and a marriage place is missing the city.

**Source:** "Quebec, Vital and Church Records (Drouin Collection), 1621–1968"

The indexed marriage date shows **9 June 1845**; the profile records **9 June 1849**. ## Source Audit — 4 sources attached, 2 findings

### Finding 1 — Indexing error (keep attached, fix the index)
**Minnesota Death Index, 1908–2002**

The index records a death year of **1954**; the profile says **1945**. The month and day (10 June) match exactly, and the birth year (1875, Norway) and death place (Erskine, Polk, Minnesota) are both correct. A one-year discrepancy in a record where every other field aligns is a classic transcription error in the index.

This collection is index-only — there is no scan inside it. **Next step:** consult the original Minnesota death certificate to confirm the correct year, then submit a correction through FamilySearch's index-correction path. Leave the source attached; the record is clearly about this person.

---

**Minnesota State Census, 1885**

The indexed person is born **1852** in Norway, heads a household with wife **Bergit** and son **Nils** in **Aurdal, Otter Tail County**. Christian P. Hole was born in **1875** — he would have been ten years old in 1885 and could not have been a household head. The birth year is off by 23 years, the county is different (Otter Tail vs. Polk), the wife's name doesn't match (Bergit vs. Inger), and the son's name doesn't match (Nils vs. Ole C.).

**Next step:** Detach this source from KD96-TV2. It belongs to KD96-WX7.

---

All three readable indexed sources (HOLE-001, HOLE-002, HOLE-003) were read with record_read using ARKs extracted from their source URLs. source_attachments was called with the HOLE-003 URI before the misattribution recommendation, confirming attachment to both KD96-TV2 and KD96-WX7. person_read(KD96-WX7) was called to confirm the true subject's facts fit the 1885 record. person_warnings was called once with correct projectPath and personId. The response names KD96-WX7 as the record's true subject only after reading that person's profile, not on attachment alone.

dimensions.name: Coverage and honesty about what was not checked
dimensions.rationale: All four attached sources are accounted for. SD-HOLE-A (1900 Census, HOLE-001) was read and judged as within ordinary variance. SD-HOLE-B (Minnesota Death Index, HOLE-002) was read and identified as an indexing error. SD-HOLE-C (1885 Census, HOLE-003) was read and identified as misattributed. SD-HOLE-D (uploaded memory) is explicitly named and reported as unreadable with the reason: 'contributor-uploaded memory with no readable record ARK.' The response does not describe any source as clean without a tool response behind it.
